Admin console first increment (TASK-801, TASK-802). Async web server via ESPAsyncWebServer 1.2.4-fork + AsyncTCP 1.1.4, served at http://192.168.4.1 and http://nomadlink.local, with the seven-section navigation (Dashboard, Network, Camera, Location, Cloud, SMS, Telephony). Only measured values are served: SoftAP/DHCP state, PPP addresses, CSQ + operator + SAMPLE AGE, NAPT state, byte and forwarded-packet counters, heap/PSRAM/flash, and real MAC/IP client pairs from esp_wifi_ap_get_sta_list_with_ip(). A client with no lease shows 'no address yet'. Six sections are explicitly NOT INTEGRATED and name their owning TASK. The web task never touches the UART: modem telemetry is sampled once before the PPP dial and cached, and the UI shows the sample age. Process fix: the product sketch had NO compile gate at all (build-baseline.sh loops firmware/baseline/* only), so added scripts/project-tracker/build-product.sh and 'make product', now part of 'make check'. Product sketch compiles at 989,467 B (32% of the 3 MB app partition). Browser pre-flight against a MOCK /api/status confirmed rendering, tab isolation, tab persistence across reload, zero external assets, and correct degraded paths -- this is a pre-flight on the HTML and is NOT hardware evidence; TEST-801 and TEST-101 remain NOT_RUN. ADR-007 records the decision and, explicitly, that the console has no authentication and is a test surface only (TASK-404 deferred). Two spec deviations recorded rather than absorbed per ADR-002: the captive portal is impossible (no lwIP DNS server, so no probe interception point) and the DHCP pool is .2-12 not .2-254 (core ships CONFIG_LWIP_DHCPS_MAX_STATION_NUM=8).

Selectable uplink + admin console on the core WebServer (TASK-102, TASK-801). AP moved from WIFI_AP to WIFI_AP_STA so a WiFi uplink can exist alongside PPP. Uplink choice (4g|wifi) and WiFi credentials persist in the gateway's own NVS and are reapplied on boot. New endpoints: GET /api/scan, POST /api/uplink/mode, POST /api/uplink/wifi, POST /api/uplink/wifi/disconnect, each surfaced as controls in the Network tab. Switching is netif_set_default() only -- lwIP routes and NAPT translates in both cases, and no route or NAT rule is hand-rolled. Two guards: a WiFi uplink with no address is refused rather than black-holing clients, and a dropped STA cannot remain the default. CRITICAL REVERSAL: ESPAsyncWebServer was replaced with the core WebServer. AsyncTCP calls raw lwIP and this core builds lwIP with CONFIG_LWIP_CHECK_THREAD_SAFETY=y and CONFIG_LWIP_TCPIP_CORE_LOCKING_INPUT unset, so three arrangements all aborted (setup task, LOCK_TCPIP_CORE() -- which deadlocks because AsyncTCP uses a blocking tcpip_api_call() -- and a dedicated FreeRTOS task). The restriction is in the core's lwIP build, not scheduling. The esp32_nat_router reference is immune because it uses esp_http_server, not ESPAsyncWebServer, so its immunity was never evidence for AsyncTCP. Cost accepted and documented: the core WebServer is poll-driven and handles one connection at a time, so handleClient() must be called in loop() and a WiFi scan stalls the console for seconds. CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD: (a) IDF's LWIP_TCPIP_CORE_LOCKING_INPUT default is n, so the core's value was never a deviation from a safer default; (b) CONFIG_LWIP_L2_TO_L3_COPY is not a NAT or forwarding enable switch -- it copies WiFi-driver L2 buffers into fresh L3 buffers to release the fixed L2 RX pool and may affect capacity only; (c) AGENTS.md said GPIO33 for modem control was a misreading and that pins 21/42 were correct -- the opposite is now measured: firmware drives GPIO33 as a module-enable rail, the PWRKEY net does not reach this board, and PPP works on that wiring; AGENTS.md, LESSONS_LEARNED.md S5 and the PWRKEY lesson are corrected in this change; (d) the console 'default route' field was reading the PPP gateway inside the PPP-up branch and so kept advertising the PPP peer after a switch to WiFi -- it is now read from netif_default unconditionally. Build gate: make product ok, 997,971 B (32% of the 3 MB app partition) and make check green. Browser pre-flight against a MOCK /api/status verified rendering, both mode buttons, scan, join, the refusal when no address, and the default-route label tracking the active uplink -- this is a pre-flight on the HTML only and is NOT hardware evidence. Nothing is recorded as hardware-verified here: no forwarding, no DHCP lease, no client internet and no mode switch have been measured on hardware in this increment. ADR-008 supersedes ADR-007 decision 1; L-15 added.

Product firmware base replaced with vendored upstream esp32_nat_router 2.4.17 (commit 2fe7a4c), built with ESP-IDF 5.5.x (ADR-009, supersedes ADR-005/007/008). WHY: a prototype was written that reproduced feature for feature a system that already exists and was already running on this board. Hand-rolling it re-implemented ip_napt_enable() routing, DHCP, the packet hooks and the console -- and walked back into the exact defect ADR-008 records, because the Arduino port's ESPAsyncWebServer drives lwIP from the wrong thread while the reference uses esp_http_server. The base inherits proven forwarding, NAT, DHCP, ACL, WireGuard, port mapping and per-client statistics. WHERE: firmware/nat_router, vendored verbatim with provenance in firmware/nat_router/README.md. TOOLCHAIN CONSTRAINT: the base does NOT build on IDF 6.x -- main requires component 'json', which moved into the component manager, giving "Failed to resolve component 'json' required by component 'main': unknown name". That is a toolchain mismatch, not a code fault; IDF 5.5.4 was installed at ~/esp/esp-idf-5.5.4 and the base builds clean for esp32s3 at 0x14f970 / 1374576 bytes. Installing it also required SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at certifi, because this machine's system python cannot verify TLS unaided. GATE: make product now builds this tree and skips cleanly when no 5.5.x install is present, so a missing toolchain cannot pass as success. The first version of that gate was wrong twice -- it grepped the log instead of checking the exit code, and it ran idf.py from the repo root, so it reported "ok" having built nothing; both are fixed and the gate is now proven to reject a broken tree (invalid C appended to main/portmap.c -> exit 1 naming file and line, reverted, clean rebuild). .gitignore had *.bin, which would have silently excluded the web installer's four firmware parts from git, leaving a published manifest whose payloads all 404; an explicit exception was added for docs/project/firmware/*.bin. WEB INSTALLER: added to docs/project/index.html, generated by render.py from the new docs/project/firmware.json (JSON authoritative, HTML generated, ADR-003) using esp-web-tools and a manifest for ESP32-S3 at the upstream offsets. Verified in Chrome: the custom element is defined, the manifest attribute is set, the button renders, and manifest plus all four parts return HTTP 200 at the declared offsets. The page is explicitly labelled base-only, with A7670E 4G, GNSS, camera and SD absent. The actual flash is NOT TESTED -- Web Serial needs a real user click and a connected board, and no device was touched. LICENCE (RISK-011, S2): upstream ships no LICENSE file and GitHub reports license=null, so redistribution rights are unstated; only the bundled WireGuard submodule is explicitly BSD-licensed. An earlier draft of firmware.json wrongly asserted GPL-3.0 and was corrected. No release may be called a production release until this is settled (Rule 37). TWO ARTIFACTS NOW EXIST and are not interchangeable: the served binary is upstream's prebuilt (1370000 B), while the local rebuild from vendored source is 1374576 B -- toolchain drift, functionally the same base; the local build replaces the served one when features land. NOT DONE: no NomadLink feature has been added to the base yet. The Arduino sketch at firmware/nomadlink is retained as historical evidence only. ADDITIONAL LESSON L-16.

Rebrand the product and its artifact; installer now serves our own build. REPORTED SYMPTOM: the flashed SSID still read ESP32_NAT_Router and the flashed file was still called esp32_nat_router.bin after both had been changed in the source. ROOT CAUSE, and it is a process failure rather than a string failure: the web installer was serving upstream's PREBUILT binaries. The page rendered, the manifest resolved, every part returned HTTP 200 and every check passed -- while the served bytes were not built from this repository at all, so no source edit could ever reach a user. A correct page serving a stale artifact is exactly the failure this project already recorded for *.bin in .gitignore, and it is the same class as 'a compile gate that reported ok having built nothing' (L-16). FIX, in four parts. (1) New scripts/project-tracker/stage-firmware.sh, exposed as 'make stage-firmware', builds the product and stages it into docs/project/firmware/, so one command owns the path from source to the bytes a user flashes and the two cannot drift silently. It asserts the four flash offsets against build_esp32s3/flash_args before copying (0x0, 0x8000, 0xf000, 0x20000): a wrong offset produces an image that flashes cleanly and then does not boot, so the offsets are checked rather than assumed. Written for bash 3.2 -- an initial mapfile version failed on this machine and the failure was the check working, not the check being optional. (2) 'make product' now WARNs when the staged payload is older than the sources it came from, naming the file, so the next drift is loud instead of invisible. (3) Artifact renamed: the IDF project is now 'nomadlink' in CMakeLists.txt, and since idf.py derives the output filename from the project name this is what turns esp32_nat_router.bin into nomadlink.bin; the manifest, staging script and both build scripts were updated in the same commit. (4) Branding: AP SSID ESP32_NAT_Router -> NomadLink, mDNS hostname esp32-nat-router -> nomadlink, web UI titles, remote-console banner, hostname field placeholder, and the upstream MCP bridge script. The MQTT topic prefix stays esp32_nat_router on purpose -- it is a functional broker identifier, not branding, and renaming it would break existing subscriptions. VERIFIED BY SCANNING THE STAGED PAYLOAD, NOT THE SOURCE, because that distinction is the whole bug: in docs/project/firmware/nomadlink.bin 'NomadLink' occurs 4 times and 'ESP32 NAT Router', 'ESP32_NAT_Router' and 'esp32-nat-router' occur 0 times. Page check in Chrome: element defined, manifest resolves, all four parts 200 (17664 / 3072 / 8192 / 1374544 bytes), old esp32_nat_router.bin now 404s, and the rendered page contains no occurrence of the old brand. The one remaining 'esp32_nat_router' string on the page is deliberate attribution in the provenance line ('Built from the vendored esp32_nat_router 2.4.17 source'). NOT TESTED: no device was flashed; Web Serial needs a real user click and a connected board. Flashing remains unverified.

BASE FIRMWARE VERIFIED ON HARDWARE; tagged NAT_ROUTER_WORKING. The project owner flashed the vendored esp32_nat_router base from the published web installer and confirmed the device broadcasts 'NomadLink'. This is the first successful flash of product firmware from this repository and it closes the open question of whether the served payload actually reaches the device -- the thing two earlier defects (a prebuilt payload no source edit could reach, then 20 un-pushed commits) had left unproven. Evidence is an independent observer's report, TEST-810, not a marker printed by our own code. Repository-side corroboration at the same time: published page HTTP 200 with 'Connect & Install' (20479 B), manifest 200, and all four parts 200 at their declared offsets (17664 / 3072 / 8192 / 1374544 B), with esp32_nat_router.bin correctly 404ing. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, kept deliberately narrow: what is proven is that the base boots, the SSID is correct, and the delivery path works. Forward throughput, DHCP lease and client internet access are NOT measured. No 4G, GNSS, camera or SD capability is in this image and none is claimed.
